title: Roundtables: Inside the Quest for Cognitive Immortality
gist: Promotional teaser for a subscriber-only MIT Technology Review roundtable in which Antonio Regalado and Mary Beth Griggs discuss efforts to extend the mind beyond death, including gradual brain replacement and uploading memories to the cloud; the page carries little substantive detail beyond the session description and related-story links.

insights.claim: Some technologists are pursuing 'cognitive immortality' — ways to keep a person's brain or mind going even beyond death, aiming for continuity of the self.
insights.speaker: MIT Technology Review
insights.so_what: Signals a fringe but media-visible neurotech/longevity niche worth watching for early-stage startup and funding activity.
insights.quote: some far-thinking technologists are working on ways to keep your brain going—even beyond death
insights.locator: In an effort to reach an elusive continuity of the self

insights.claim: Two candidate paths to mind preservation highlighted by MIT Technology Review editors are gradual brain replacement and uploading memories to the cloud.
insights.speaker: MIT Technology Review
insights.so_what: Frames the two technical routes (biological replacement vs. digital upload) along which any investable neurotech/longevity ventures would sit.
insights.quote: including gradual brain replacement and uploading our memories to the cloud
insights.locator: Science editor Mary Beth Griggs and senior editor for biomedicine Antonio Regalado

insights.claim: Technology that lets people simulate 'speaking' to deceased relatives has arrived, according to a related MIT Technology Review story headline, raising open questions about readiness.
insights.speaker: MIT Technology Review
insights.so_what: Grief-tech / digital-afterlife AI is already a commercial product category, with societal acceptance still unsettled.
insights.quote: Technology that lets us “speak” to our dead relatives has arrived. Are we ready?

insights.claim: A stealthy startup reportedly pitched the idea of brainless human clones, per a related MIT Technology Review story headline linked to the cognitive-immortality roundtable.
insights.speaker: MIT Technology Review
insights.so_what: Shows how far-out longevity concepts are being pitched to investors; expect ethical and regulatory scrutiny.
insights.quote: Inside the stealthy startup that pitched brainless human clones

insights.claim: New studies cast doubt on the rejuvenation idea that transplanting young organs acts as a fountain of youth for recipients.
insights.speaker: MIT Technology Review
insights.so_what: Tempers enthusiasm for young-tissue/young-organ rejuvenation theses within the longevity sector.
insights.quote: New studies pour cold water on a prominent rejuvenation idea.
insights.locator: Young organs may not be a fountain of youth for recipients

insights.claim: An AI 'mind-reading' tool can reconstruct what a person is looking at from a brain scan, and scientists hope it could eventually reconstruct inner thoughts, mental images, or dreams.
insights.speaker: MIT Technology Review
insights.so_what: AI-driven neural decoding is advancing, relevant to brain-computer interface and neuroimaging players.

insights.claim: The PRIMA implant system can restore sight for patients with advanced macular degeneration (AMD), enabling them to read and do crosswords.
insights.speaker: MIT Technology Review
insights.so_what: A concrete neuroprosthetic with functional outcomes — watch the developer and retinal-implant market for commercialization.
insights.quote: The PRIMA system lets people with advanced AMD read and do crosswords.
insights.locator: This implant can restore sight for patients with macular degeneration

insights.claim: Side effects of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are still being characterized, including possible effects on hair, nails, and vision.
insights.speaker: MIT Technology Review
insights.so_what: Ongoing side-effect questions are a tail risk to monitor for GLP-1 drug makers.
insights.quote: Could the drugs affect hair, nails, and vision?
insights.locator: We’re still figuring out the side effects of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs
